label: Sealed stores: which data files are kept encrypted at rest, and where their key lives

params.name: files
params.label: Stores (data/<name>.json) written sealed - credentials and AI keys. A plain file of these names still reads and is sealed at its next save

params.name: key_env
params.label: The environment variable that may hold the seal key itself (a Fernet key) - wins over the key file

params.name: key_file_env
params.label: The environment variable naming the key file's path

params.name: key_file
params.label: With no path set: this file BESIDE the data folder (never inside it, so a backup of data/ alone opens nothing); made once, owner-only

params.name: marker
params.label: The one field a sealed file holds on disk

params.name: words

default.no_key: data/{name}.json is sealed and its seal key is not at {path} (nor in env {env}) - put the seal key back (DEPLOY.md, Seal key) and restart. Nothing was changed.
default.wrong_key: data/{name}.json is sealed with another seal key than the one at {path} - put the right key back (DEPLOY.md, Seal key) and restart. Nothing was changed.

params.label: What the store says when a sealed file cannot be opened

description_nl: DomainTemplate 2026-11-18 gap audit C1-11: credentials and AI keys were plain JSON at rest. core/store.py seals the files named here with Fernet (cryptography, already locked); the key comes from env key_env, else the file env key_file_env names, else key_file beside the data folder (made once, mode 600, only while no sealed file exists). A sealed file that cannot be opened is never read as empty and never overwritten: the store raises with words.no_key / words.wrong_key. smtp is not listed: deploy/demo/setup.sh copies prod's smtp.json to a demo that has no prod key.

words.no_key: data/{name}.json is sealed and its seal key is not at {path} (nor in env {env}) - put the seal key back (DEPLOY.md, Seal key) and restart. Nothing was changed.
words.wrong_key: data/{name}.json is sealed with another seal key than the one at {path} - put the right key back (DEPLOY.md, Seal key) and restart. Nothing was changed.
